result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_diameter()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get graph diameter (maximum eccentricity). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16996-L17037){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_diameter(unconnected=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The diameter is the longest shortest path between any two nodes. This metric is useful for understanding the "width" of a network. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, computes maximum diameter across all connected components. If `False`, returns `None` for disconnected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maximum distance between any two nodes, or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate diameter of a path: ::: {#11844aef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) # Returns 3 (A to D) graph.get_diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
